subject: Revenge is already updated
author: ZombieTron
body:
Revenge got it's updated version on the 360.  There were quite a few changes made from the Original Xbox version.

I have taken this list of changes from Jasman's featured article Burnout: Generations;

Gameplay changes compared to Burnout Revenge

  • The Launch meter has been removed from Crash Junctions
  • All cars are now unlocked for online play even if they haven’t been unlocked in offline mode
  • Burnout Clips introduced – BurnoutAholics can now save 30 second clips of any offline event played and can share these clips through Xbox Live
  • Online Revenge Rivals introduced – The system now keeps track of the number of times a player has been taken out by or has taken out any given player. This number is reset every time the score is settled. Settling the score means that you take down someone that has takedowns on you. The number of times you have settled the score with a player sometimes is displayed before a race is started. When you have settled the score more than 100 times with the same player he or she will become your nemesis
  • Downloadable content has been added to the game (in the form of 7 downloadable cars)

And I think the 360 version is a lot better then the original, although there were no new tracks added, but then new tracks (or the island) isn't coming to Paradise for another few months yet.  I would love to see new tracks in Revenge, but only if they were as perfect as the tracks we already have. 🙂

--- The Original and the Best ---

subject: Revenge on XBOX 360
author: Xandu
body:
A special version of Burnout Revenge was released for the XBox 360 in March 2006. You can read about some of the changes here. The 360 version of Revenge also supports HD. As I said there are still a lot of people playing this game online and there are still new players coming online. It seems like the game is still selling quite well.

Burnout Revenge (XBOX 1 and PS2) was taken offline by EA in September 2007 because there was not enough players online. I think Revenge for Original Xbox had something like 10 players online a day at this point. When we talked to EA their official explanation was either that number of players online was too low for these games or that they were freeing up resources on the servers to get ready for Burnout Paradise.

-- The Creator --

subject: Xbox 360 HHD
author: Xandu
body:
So far the 20GB HDD has been large enough for me so I have not looked into what kind of modifications can be done. Also I think most new xbox 360 comes with either no hard drive, 60GB or 120GB. The 60 GB XBox 360 sells for around £150 so I dont think it is worth the risk or hassle trying to mess with the harddrive.

It is also worth mentioning that the 360 supports streaming so you can stream media (video, music, pictures) from your PC (does not have to be media center) to your 360. It supports most formats incliuding xvid. This really reduces the need for a big HDD. It is also possible to connect most external USB hdds (read only).

When you get a new XBox live membership you automatically get one month of gold for free. After one month this is changed into a silver membership that you at any time can upgrade to gold (either using credit card or redeeming a code). You need gold to play online. A 12 month subscription (price from play.com) costs around £35.

-- The Creator --
